newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Bhutto proposes conference on Kashmir,arms control.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto proposes conference on Kashmir,arms control.

text.p: Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto proposed a conference on Thursday involving India and major powers to resolve the Kashmir dispute, promote conventional arms control and arrest the danger of a nuclear arms race in South Asia.

"I believe that such multilateral talks offer a framework for genuine negotiations which can lead to resolution of disputes, arrest the nuclear threat and promote prosperity in South Asia," she said in a speech to the General Assembly.

She also warned that, just as Pakistan was prepared to sign any nuclear treaties if India also signed simultaneously, "any step of nuclear escalation by our neighbor will find a response from us to preserve our national security."

"I would like to take this opportunity to propose to this august Assembly that it endorse the convening of a multilateral dialogue for peace and security in South Asia, including the participation of not only Pakistan and India, but of the five permanent members of the Security Council and other major powers like Germany and Japan," Bhutto said.

The conference could cover three critical areas, she added -- the resolution of the Kashmir dispute, the promotion of conventional arms control and confidence building measures and measures to promote nuclear restraint and arrest the danger of a nuclear arms race in South Asia."

Such multilateral talks offered a framework for genuine negotiations which could lead to "resolution of disputes, arrest the nuclear threat and promote prosperity in South Asia. And I hope that this proposal will evoke support in this Assembly and from India," she added.
